projectDescription:
The BlueMX Atlalpan Blue Carbon Project is a grouped project restoring degraded tidal mangrove wetlands in the Sistema Lagunar de Alvarado, Veracruz, Mexico, for climate mitigation, biodiversity, resilience, and community livelihoods. It applies VM0033 v2.1.

The project area is former mangrove converted to pasture (Moreno-Casasola et al., 2002; Portilla-Ochoa, 2003; Ruiz-Fernández et al., 2014). Tidal canals are silted or blocked by livestock embankments, and dry-season fires and invasive Typha domingensis degrade it further. Without the project, a self-reinforcing cycle of grazing, invasive spread, and wildfire would keep preventing mangrove recovery.

The start date is 29 April 2022, when restoration work began. Project activities include desilting tidal canals to restore water flow; building raised nuclei (chinampas) to create suitable sites for seedlings; planting locally adapted Rhizophora mangle, Laguncularia racemosa, and Avicennia germinans; controlling Typha domingensis to reduce competition with young mangroves; and installing firebreaks and cattle fencing to protect restored areas. These actions increase carbon stocks in aboveground biomass, belowground biomass, and soil.

Ex-ante net removals over the 28.75-year first crediting period are 385,149 tCO₂e (13,396 tCO₂e/yr) for the 976 ha in the two initial PAIs and 3,913,885 tCO₂e (136,135 tCO₂e/yr) for the total restorable area of 10,064 ha

projectName: Mianning1 Water Management with Rice Cultivation
projectDescription: The project carried out changes from a continuously flooded regime to an intermittently flooded regime during rice cultivation in Fengqing County and Yongde County, Yunnan Province, China, with a total acreage of 11,247 ha of double-cropping rice. Without the project, there would be no ditches, pumps, valves, and reservoirs to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario in which rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded conditions can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittently flooded method is more conducive to saving water, increasing rice yield, and reducing methane emissions than the continuously flooded method.
